en.name: Oregano, fresh
en.summary: Fresh oregano keeps 1–2 weeks at room temperature with its stems in water, or 2–3 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. It has small, tough, slightly woody leaves, which is why it holds up longer than a thin-leafed herb like coriander.
en.pantry: 1–2 weeks with the stems trimmed and standing in a little water, out of direct sun and with the water changed daily. Oregano is a Mediterranean herb with firm, somewhat resinous leaves, and it copes with dry air far better than the soft herbs do. If anything, the failure at room temperature is drying rather than rotting — the sprigs simply become dried oregano, which is not a disaster and is in fact how most oregano is used.
en.fridge: 2–3 weeks at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, wrapped loosely in dry kitchen paper inside a bag or box in the crisper. Do not wash it until you cook. Because the leaves are small and sit close to the stem, any moisture trapped between them stays there, so a bunch sealed wet in a bag turns black in days. Check it every few days and strip off any blackened leaves. Fresh oregano bruises less easily than basil, so it survives the crisper drawer better than most.
en.freezer: Freeze damage will appear, so no freezer timeline is given. Frozen oregano leaves darken and go limp, though the flavour holds better than in most herbs because so much of it sits in resinous oils rather than in delicate volatiles. The more useful route for oregano is the traditional one: hang a bunch upside down somewhere dry and airy and let it dry properly, then strip the leaves into a jar. Dried oregano is a genuinely good ingredient rather than a consolation prize.
en.thawing: Do not thaw. Add frozen sprigs or leaves straight to a hot pan or a sauce.
spoilage: Blackened leaves, usually where moisture was trapped against the stem.
A sour or musty smell instead of a peppery, resinous one.
Slime at the cut ends or on the lower leaves.
Mould on the stems in a tightly closed bag.
tips: Strip the leaves from the woody stems before chopping; the stems stay tough.
Do not wash until you use it; trapped water between small leaves is what blackens a bunch.
Dry a surplus bunch upside down rather than freezing it.
Oregano stands up to long cooking, unlike most soft herbs — add it early.

faq.q: How long does fresh oregano keep?
faq.a: 1–2 weeks at room temperature with the stems in water, or 2–3 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
Freeze damage will appear, so no timeline is given. The leaves darken and go limp, though the flavour survives. Drying a surplus bunch is usually the better option.

faq.q: Should oregano go in early or late in cooking?
faq.a: Early. Unlike basil or coriander, its flavour sits in resinous oils that stand up to long cooking.

zh.name: 新鮮奧勒岡
zh.summary: 新鮮奧勒岡把莖插在水裡放常溫可放 1～2 週，放 4 °C 以下冷藏則是 2～3 週。它的葉片小而堅韌、略帶木質，所以比香菜那種薄葉香草耐放。
zh.pantry: 把莖剪一下、插進一點水裡，避免直曬，每天換水，1～2 週。奧勒岡是地中海香草，葉片結實、帶點樹脂感，對乾燥空氣的耐受度遠勝軟莖香草。真要說，它在常溫下的結局是「乾掉」而不是「爛掉」——枝條會自己變成乾燥奧勒岡，而那並不是災難，事實上奧勒岡大多就是這樣被使用的。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下 2～3 週：用乾的廚房紙巾鬆鬆包好，裝進袋子或盒子放蔬果室。要下鍋時才洗。因為葉片小、又緊貼著莖，夾在葉間的水氣會一直留在那裡，所以一把濕著密封的奧勒岡幾天內就會發黑。每隔幾天檢查一次，把發黑的葉子摘掉。奧勒岡比羅勒不容易壓傷，所以在蔬果室裡的存活率比多數香草好。
zh.freezer: 冷凍會出現凍傷，所以沒有給期限。冷凍過的奧勒岡葉會變深、變軟，不過它的風味比多數香草留得住，因為它的味道大半在樹脂類精油裡，而不是在纖細的揮發性成分裡。對奧勒岡來說，更實用的路是傳統做法：把一束倒掛在乾燥通風的地方好好陰乾，再把葉子剝進罐子。乾燥奧勒岡是真正好用的食材，不是退而求其次的安慰獎。
zh.thawing: 不要解凍。冷凍的枝葉直接丟進熱鍋或醬汁裡。
spoilage: 葉子發黑，通常出現在水氣被困在貼近莖的地方。
聞起來酸或有霉味，而不是帶胡椒感的樹脂香。
切口或下段葉子變得黏滑。
tips: 切之前先把葉子從木質的莖上剝下來；莖不會變軟。
要用時才洗；小葉片之間困住的水正是讓整把發黑的原因。
多出來的整束倒掛陰乾，比冷凍好。
和多數軟莖香草不同，奧勒岡耐久煮——可以早點下。

faq.q: 新鮮奧勒岡可以放多久？
faq.a: 莖插水放常溫 1～2 週，或 4 °C 以下冷藏 2～3 週。

faq.q: 新鮮奧勒岡可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 冷凍會凍傷，所以沒有給期限。葉子會變深變軟，但風味留得住。多出來的一束拿去陰乾通常是更好的選擇。

faq.q: 奧勒岡該早下還是晚下？
faq.a: 早下。和羅勒或香菜不同，它的風味在耐得住久煮的樹脂類精油裡。
